description.value: Backcountry campground in E.C. Manning Park near the northern terminus of the Pacific Crest Trail at the Canada-US border; hike-in only (more than 1 km from any road), so inaccessible to loaded touring bikes. A permit ($5/person/night) is required but no advance reservation needed.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website confirms Monument 78 as one of several designated backcountry campgrounds within E.C. Manning Park, listed by name alongside Buckhorn, Kicking Horse, and others. The website explicitly states that Monument 78 is not among the three campgrounds that accept peak-season reservations (Buckhorn, Kicking Horse, and Frosty Creek), and that 'most backcountry campgrounds do not accept reservations,' supporting a false value for that amenity. No amenity-level details specific to Monument 78 (water, shelter, food storage, etc.) appear anywhere in the website content, so those fields remain null.
concerns: OSM record has no phone number; phone field populated from BC Parks general contact page (1-800-689-9025), not from an OSM-sourced value.
The linked website covers all E.C. Manning backcountry campgrounds collectively — no dedicated page exists for Monument 78, so amenity-level details could not be confirmed.
Backcountry location more than 1 km from any road may limit accessibility to loaded cycle tourists depending on trail surface and portage requirements; primarily suitable for bikepacking.
No physical address available; GPS coordinates are the sole locator for this site.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Monument 78 is an active, legitimate BC Parks backcountry campground on a significant wilderness corridor (Pacific Crest Trail) within E.C. Manning Park; it is a genuine overnight option for bikepacking and adventure cyclists traversing this region.
enrichment_extras.notes: Monument 78 takes its name from the international boundary monument marking the Canada-US border at the 49th parallel. An overnight backcountry permit is mandatory (register at camping.bcparks.ca or call 1-800-689-9025); no advance reservation is required for this specific campground. Nearest public phones and services are at Manning Park Resort on Highway 3.
